Aluminum nanoparticles (ANPs) are among the most energy-dense solid fuels, yet the atomic mechanisms governing their transition from passivated particles to highly reactive states remain elusive. This stems from a fundamental computational bottleneck: Ab initio methods offer quantum-level fidelity but are restricted to small spatiotemporal scales (<500 atoms, picoseconds), while empirical force fields lack the reactive fidelity required for complex combustion environments. Here, we bridge this gap by employing a human-audited, multiagent framework to make the development and validation of a task-specific machine learning potential (MLP) more traceable and auditable. The workflow coordinates active learning, model evaluation, validation evidence, and human expert review, while leaving scientific interpretation and model-use decisions under researcher control. This collaborative cycle ensures quantum mechanical accuracy while exhibiting near-linear scalability. Strikingly, our simulations reveal a temperature-regulated dual-mode oxidation mechanism: At moderate temperatures, the oxide shell acts as a dynamic "gatekeeper," regulating oxidation through a "breathing mode" of transient nanochannels; above a critical threshold, a "rupture mode" leads to shell failure and rapid combustion. Importantly, we resolve a decades-old controversy by demonstrating that aluminum cation outward diffusion, rather than oxygen transport, dominates mass transfer in studied regimes, with diffusion coefficients consistently exceeding those of oxygen by 2 to 3 orders of magnitude. These results provide an atomistic framework for interpreting ANP reactivity and illustrate how human-audited agentic workflows can make domain-specific reactive MLP development and deployment more reproducible.

To improve task performance while encouraging desirable response properties, LLM post-training often combines a primary reward (e.g., correctness) with auxiliary rewards (e.g., brevity or efficiency). However, how these rewards are aggregated can critically affect training outcomes. We show that symmetric aggregation, which treats reward channels equally, can induce a failure where aggregate reward improves while primary-task performance degrades, even when individual rewards are meaningful. We investigate this aggregation-induced failure through a one-step multi-reward decision formulation, characterizing when it constitutes multi-reward hacking. We prove that, under symmetric aggregation, deterministic conditional-mean GRPO converges to auxiliary-favoring behavior when auxiliary rewards are more reliably obtained, regardless of initialization. We propose Trust-Anchored Gating (TAG), which first elects an anchor channel based on the policy drift induced by optimizing each channel alone, then gates auxiliary credit on anchor satisfaction. Unlike calibration-sensitive static reweighting, TAG structurally eliminates credit for auxiliary-only outcomes while preserving additional credit for joint success. In the same analytical setting, TAG provably reverses this selection, converging to the primary-favoring action from any initialization when the primary channel is anchored. Experiments across Qwen and Llama models on mathematics and program synthesis reveal substantial degradation under symmetric, constrained, and normalized aggregation, whereas TAG mitigates this failure. On Qwen3-4B with a brevity reward, TAG achieves 0.581 pass@4 versus 0.220 for additive aggregation, while shortening responses by 44% relative to correctness-only training.

Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being adopted as teaching tools in computing education, particularly for developing AI tutors capable of answering student questions. With the rise in enrollment of international students in computing programs, researchers have begun to explore the difficulties that non-native English speaker (NNES) students face in computing courses due to language barriers. To aid such students, we developed a general-purpose AI tutor system that can process student questions in foreign languages (currently focused on Mandarin) and provide bilingual responses. Our system also incorporates the functionality of generating a glossary of technical terms and their explanations to enhance comprehension. Our approach utilizes a specialized Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline with a novel question extraction mechanism, enabling us to effectively utilize a diverse array of course materials for answering student queries. We evaluated our AI tutor using 91 Piazza posts, demonstrating that it could answer 83.52% of the posts correctly and in a helpful manner. The tutor also provided high-quality translations for 76.92% of the questions and generated technical term glossaries for 64.47% of them. Our findings underscore the potential of multi-source RAG pipeline in enhancing AI tutor systems, offering support for non-native speakers that are challenging to provide with traditional supporting staff of a computing course.
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

documents.abstract: As large language models become increasingly capable of generating, and assisting with, scientific writing, there is a need for greater transparency and disclosure around the use of AI in research. Consequently, a veritable subfield of research and a number of commercial services aim to flag AI-generated content automatically. However, existing detectors which rely only on text extracted from PDFs fail to benefit from the rich visual information contained in the formatting of math-heavy scientific content. To study this, we select human-written proof and prose passages from pre-2022 arXiv LaTeX sources and re-generate them using 15 modern LLMs within the context of the same paper. This leaves us with coupled human and AI outputs in three different representations: the LaTeX source, a rendered image of the PDF, and the text extracted from the PDF. We find that the accuracy of the state-of-the-art Pangram 4 drops significantly as the mathematical content in a passage increases, especially when evaluated on text as opposed to LaTeX. However, this is not an inherent limitation of detecting AI-generated math: finetuning Qwen-3.5-27B based detectors on this domain recovers the gap, with LaTeX inputs performing significantly better than text since they preserve more formatting information. Since LaTeX sources are rarely available in practice, we also train SnapJudge: an image-based detector operating on screenshots of both prose and proofs from papers. At 0.1% false positive rate, SnapJudge achieves a detection rate of 92% on proofs and 93% on prose generated by frontier models, substantially outperforming both Pangram 4 and our text-based detector. We release our data, models and code at https://nlplab.cs.duke.edu/snapjudge.

Decision trees can make vision-language model (VLM) classification interpretable by replacing a single prediction with a sequence of root-to-leaf questions. However, the accuracy cost of this greedy, non-backtracking procedure remains unclear. We introduce \textbf{MYOPIA}, a benchmark comprising four LLM-generated, human-refined decision trees for GTSRB, MNIST, CIFAR-10, and MSCOCO, together with matched prompts, diagnostic protocols, and an evaluation harness. Across GPT-4o, Qwen-VL Max, and LLaMA-3.2 11B Vision, tree traversal underperforms zero-shot prompting in all 12 dataset--model pairs; paired bootstrap analyses consistently favor zero-shot. Our diagnostics characterize interacting failure modes associated with this gap. Models often recall tree-encoded class attributes more accurately than they ground the same attributes in images: the mean label--image accuracy gaps are 9.5, 13.8, and 12.6 points for GPT-4o, Qwen-VL Max, and LLaMA, respectively. Incorrect local decisions then irreversibly exclude the correct class, while answer extraction introduces additional model-dependent loss. A node-level audit of the four trees finds that split entropy is weakly but consistently associated with lower node accuracy, whereas depth, branching factor, and within-node grounding differences are less stable. \textbf{MYOPIA} therefore provides a framework for diagnosing hierarchical visual classification and motivates testing tree designs that prioritize perceptual answerability and recovery from early errors. Code is available at https://github.com/islammesabah/VLM_Classification.

Navigating Change: Emerging Perspectives on Business, Economy, Technology and Society is an edited academic volume that explores emerging developments and transformations across business, economics, technology and society. The book brings together scholarly contributions on digital transformation, generative artificial intelligence, digital marketing, consumer behaviour, retail innovation, sustainable growth, healthcare, education, financial decision-making and investment behaviour. It examines the opportunities, challenges and implications of technological and economic change for organisations, individuals and communities. Through conceptual discussions, literature-based analyses and empirical studies, this volume presents interdisciplinary perspectives on innovation, sustainability, organisational development and changing societal practices. This book is intended for students, research scholars, academicians, educators, business professionals and readers interested in contemporary developments in business, economics, technology and society. Editors: Dr. Jithin Scaria, Dr. Praveen K. P., Dr. Amrapali D. Gosavi, Dr. Prakasha Rao A., and Dr. Sanjay P. Dhangar. Publisher: Right Skills Academic SolutionsEdition: First Edition, 2026ISBN: 978-81-994950-8-1

The study of human behaviour in prehistoric societies is a primary objective of archaeological and anthropological research. One way to investigate past behaviour is through the analysis of technological organisation. The resolution at which archaeologists can examine the past is highly dependent on the sedimentary dynamics and site-formation processes that play a key role in the preservation of the archaeological record. To mitigate the limitations inherent in the archaeological record, lithic refitting has emerged as a valuable method to enhance the contextual resolution of Palaeolithic sites. However, this method has not been uniformly applied to assess the impact of syn -postdepositional processes in archaeology. Cova Gran de Santa Linya (NE Iberia) preserves evidence of long-term sedimentary and erosive cycles that have shaped the differential preservation of archaeological evidence. This is exemplified by unit 7P (20.5 k −18 k cal BP), located in the Platform Sector, which has been partially affected by erosive processes within the site, resulting in complex vertical and horizontal stratigraphic relationships within the site’s Last Glacial Maximum sequence. To assess the impact of natural and anthropogenic disturbances on Level 7P, we conducted lithic refitting and technological analysis, combined with spatial data. Refittings indicated the lithic assemblage remained unaffected by erosive events at the site, reinforcing the in situ preservation of the occupation. The spatial distribution revealed a dense cluster of refitted artefacts in 2 m 2 . Refitting within this cluster revealed highly specialised and complex behaviours associated with microblade production. Archaeostratigraphic, spatial, technological and contextual data were combined to assess whether this accumulation is the result of anthropogenic or natural factors. We have also investigated what human activities underlying the formation of lithic clusters. The main cluster of 7P, in conjunction with other elements of the archaeological record facilitates the identification of spatial organisational patterns characterised by short-distance intra-site mobility. Overall, we highlight systematic refitting as valuable holistic approach for enhancing contextual resolution in archaeological assemblages, thereby refining our understanding of the natural and human factors involved in the formation of Palaeolithic sites.

This study examines how cinema students attribute authorship during AI-assisted screenwriting and how those judgments relate to creative decisions. Drawing on a fourteen-week, design-based course, it compares logbooks with 436 student turns across twenty generative-AI conversations. In four of six co-writing cases, students selected and retained system-originated material. The clearest tension appeared when students claimed the idea as their own but assigned the text entirely to AI while repeatedly rejecting generated material, a response the instrument’s own categories leave ambiguous. Read against Livingston, Gaut and Sellors, these cases show that textual generation, creative decision-making and authorship attribution can diverge within one process. Cinema education should ask not only who authored a text, but on what basis.

topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Abstract—The continuous scaling of conventional Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) on classical Von Neumann architectures has reached severe physical boundaries governed by the 'memory wall' and unsustainable thermal dissipation. Battery-constrained edge computing environments—including autonomous micro-robotics, bio-implantable telemetry, and space-borne remote sensing—demand continuous, milliwatt-scale machine perception that standard GPUs and digital tensor accelerators cannot deliver. Neuromorphic Computing and Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) establish an alternative non-Von Neumann computing paradigm inspired by biological neurobiology, processing information via sparse, event-driven temporal spikes rather than dense, continuous matrix multiplications. However, deploying high-performance SNNs across resource-constrained edge hardware introduces profound foundational challenges: non-differentiable threshold activation dynamics that complicate gradient-based training, temporal latency vs. spike sparsity trade-offs, and microarchitectural fragmentation across asynchronous neuromorphic silicon. This paper delivers an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of neuromorphic computing for ultra-low-power edge intelligence. We formalize the non-linear differential dynamics of Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) and Adaptive Exponential (AdEx) neuron models, derive the mathematical formulations of surrogate gradient backpropagation through time (BPTT), and analyze ANN-to-SNN rate-conversion bounds. Furthermore, we construct an empirical hardware testbed benchmarking neuromorphic silicon platforms (Intel Loihi 2 and SynSense Speck) against state-of-the-art edge accelerators (NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano and Google Coral Edge TPU) across neuromorphic vision (DVS-Gesture, N-MNIST) and real-time edge bio-signal classification (MIT-BIH Arrhythmia). Our experimental findings demonstrate that event-driven SNN execution on neuromorphic silicon achieves up to a 42.6x reduction in dynamic energy consumption over edge GPUs while maintaining competitive classification accuracy (within 0.8% of floating-point DNN baselines) and sub-10ms inference latencies. Finally, we formulate open research directions in memristive in-memory computing crossbars, on-chip continuous spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP), and hybrid large-scale neuromorphic foundation models.

Epilepsy is among the most burdensome neurological disorders worldwide, with an impact that extends far beyond seizure frequency alone. Depression, anxiety, cognitive impairment, and internalized stigma affect a substantial proportion of individuals with epilepsy, yet these comorbidities remain systematically undertreated in routine neurological care. Conventional psychoeducation, largely centered on passive information delivery, has shown limited effectiveness in addressing the psychological and social complexities of living with epilepsy. Neuroscience-Informed Psychoeducation for Epilepsy (NIPE) offers a fundamentally different approach: one that translates the neuroscience of seizure generation, network dysfunction, and neuroplasticity into accessible frameworks, shifting patients from passive recipients of information to active, metacognitively engaged participants in their own care.This chapter presents NIPE as both a clinical framework and an integrative layer across the continuum of epilepsy management. Beginning with the neurobiological mechanisms underlying seizures and epileptogenesis, it highlights how the same neural networks implicated in ictal activity also contribute to the psychiatric and cognitive comorbidities that shape patients’ daily experiences. It further examines how NIPE interfaces with evidence-based psychological interventions, pharmacologic education, neuromodulation, epilepsy surgery, and the management of refractory epilepsy, as well as the unique needs of women and other populations with distinct clinical considerations.In addition, the chapter explores the digital expansion of NIPE, including adaptive telehealth platforms, wearable biosensors, digital phenotyping, and the emerging role of artificial intelligence in tailoring psychoeducational delivery. Importantly, it addresses current limitations and ethical considerations with transparency, including the absence of standardized NIPE protocols and the relative scarcity of randomized controlled trials specifically within epilepsy populations.The chapter concludes with a forward-looking perspective on the infrastructure, research agenda, and cross-disciplinary collaboration required to embed NIPE into routine epileptology practice. NIPE is positioned not as an adjunct to epilepsy care, but as a unifying framework, a shared language that enables truly integrated, patient-centered care.

A new initiative convened by nonprofit software firm Blackbaud, dubbed the AI Coalition for Social Impact, is now offering a certification program designed to help nonprofit leaders and staff build the skills and governance needed to use artificial intelligence responsibly and effectively in their operations.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Unlearning aims to remove selected knowledge from large language models to mitigate privacy and safety risks while preserving useful capabilities. For models that continue to be fine-tuned after release, this goal is insufficient: they must also resist relearning the deleted knowledge while preserving plasticity, the ability to learn new tasks. Existing defenses train against simulated relearning while trying to preserve useful capabilities, but low relearning alone cannot distinguish selective resistance from a general loss of plasticity. Evaluating preservation after an update requires deciding what the updated model should remain close to. A pre-update reference penalizes useful changes induced by the update simply because they depart from earlier outputs. We therefore formulate the reference-timing hypothesis that, at comparable target suppression, an update-matched reference better preserves plasticity than a pre-update one. To test and address this hypothesis, we propose Update-Matched Unlearning (UMU), which applies the same simulated relearning update to the defended model and to an undefended reference initialized from the same unlearned model, and uses new-task learning to guide model selection. Extensive experiments on TOFU and FaithUn with Llama and Qwen models show that UMU improves both relearning resistance and plasticity across all three base unlearning methods, lowering harmful and benign relearning by 30.4 and 9.9 points on average while raising new-task accuracy by 3.5 points. When the reference does not receive the update, relearning remains similarly low but new-task accuracy falls below the base method, supporting the reference-timing hypothesis and showing that robust unlearning should prevent recovery selectively without suppressing learning itself.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Recurring expressions in model-written text are often treated as signatures of machine authorship, yet most of them serve legitimate functions. Whether such an expression is a tic depends on whether the model knows when it is called for. This judgment of appropriateness, central to communicative competence, remains largely unexamined for language models. We study it through the Mandarin corrective construction bushi X, ershi Y ("not X, but Y"). Drawing on Gricean pragmatics and corrective negation, we introduce a decision tree that classifies uses as substantive, optional, or defective by testing whether the context makes X a live alternative and whether rejecting X is informative. Five commercial models use the construction 2.5 to 9.2 times as densely as a human reference. Of 307 annotated uses, only 1.30% are defective while 52.8% are optional, that is, correct but unneeded, so models fall short in appropriateness far more often than in correctness. Several reward models favor the construction even over quality-matched variants, an LLM judge favors it even where the context does not license it, and both supervised fine-tuning and preference optimization tend to raise its frequency in open-weight models. We hope this work encourages the development of models attentive to the appropriateness of their expressions.

High-quality police response and the technically accurate drafting of Police Reports (Boletins de Ocorrência – B.O.) are fundamental pillars for ensuring access to justice and preserving the evidentiary integrity of criminal prosecution. Deficiencies in primary reception and negligent or inaccurate record-keeping pose severe obstacles to the effectiveness of the criminal justice system. The operational reality of the frontline officer, marked by institutional pressure to quickly clear radio dispatches to resume preventative patrol, coupled with system latency and poor interface ergonomics on mobile devices, acts as a primary driver of superficial records. Furthermore, while the definitive legal classification belongs strictly to the judicial police and the prosecution, the preliminary classification and factual description drafted by the military police fundamentally condition initial referrals, procedural routing, and crime analytics. This initial defect triggers a cascade effect: it leaves Civil Police detectives without actionable evidentiary leads, undermines the Public Prosecutor's ability to build robust indictments (opinio delicti), and forces the Judiciary to deny pretrial detentions or release suspects due to poorly described legal materiality. Overcoming these systemic bottlenecks requires continuous in-person training, ergonomic software re-engineering, and the institutionalization of documentary auditing routines divorced from punitive disciplinary threats, highlighting the regulatory framework implemented by the Military Police of the State of Paraná (PMPR), particularly Instruction Note nº 004/2024 - PM/3.

This article examines the role of artificial intelligence (AI) across the complete visual effects (VFX) production pipeline in contemporary cinema, emphasizing the practical integration of machine learning (ML) techniques into pre-production, production, and post-production. It argues that AI has become a set of supporting tools integrated into established VFX workflows, including camera and object tracking, rotoscoping (roto), digital paint and object removal, simulation, rendering, compositing, and final delivery, reducing operational challenges and expanding opportunities for creative experimentation. The analysis draws on technical sources (SIGGRAPH/ACM), official tool documentation, and institutional guidelines addressing professional credits, intellectual property, consent, and digital replicas. When quantitative data on time and cost savings are not publicly available in sufficient detail, this limitation is explicitly acknowledged, with emphasis placed on qualitative evidence and documented technical mechanisms.

This article discusses the growing importance of knowledge as an organizational asset and the integration between Knowledge Management (KM) and Artificial Intelligence (AI). This integration can enhance KM processes, while consistent KM practices provide high quality data for intelligent algorithms. The purpose of this study is to present how Petrobras is structuring itself to apply AI in its KM processes. This is a case study based on content analysis of documents (internal reports, consulting reports, event materials), interviews with the company’s KM team, and a literature review. The study contributes to the field by highlighting Petrobras’ journey as a complex and regulated organization. This journey involved combining agile methods, experimentation, international scouting, and other strategies to meet business requirements aligned with organizational needs, expanding the benefits of this technology. As a result, in addition to the strong ROI potential and the intangible benefits associated with applying AI to KM processes, the study concludes that this innovation represents a strategic step for Petrobras. However, success will depend on the combination of technology and human factors, ensuring that the established governance enables proper data curation and mitigation of risks associated with this emerging technology.
topics: Impact of AI and Big Data on Business and Society

documents.abstract: Aims: The study aimed to assess the occupational and ergonomic characteristics of selected bamboo and cane weaving craftsmen in Assam, with particular emphasis on workspace sitting arrangements, adopted working postures, and associated ergonomic risk. Study Design: A descriptive research design was adopted. Place and Duration of Study: The study was conducted in the Barpeta Cluster of Assam from June 2024 to July 2025. Methodology: A total of 260 craftsmen were purposively selected (n = 97 bamboo-only, n = 47 cane-only, and n = 116 bamboo-and-cane craftsmen) to assess occupational and personal characteristics. Detailed observational postural assessment and Rapid Entire Body Assessment (REBA) were conducted among a purposively selected subsample of 60 craftsmen (20 participants per activity group; 10 males and 10 females). Data were collected using a structured interview schedule and observational sheets. Associations between posture types and personal variables were examined using the chi-square test of independence and post-hoc residual analysis. Results: The mean age and work experience of the respondents were 42.88 years and 15.42 years, respectively, while the mean daily working duration was 7.48 hours. Overall, 43.46% of craftsmen worked for 6–8 hours per day and 39.23% worked for more than 8 hours. A wooden low stool/Pidha was the most commonly reported sitting arrangement during splitting (57.70%), stripping (42.30%), bending (53.80%), weaving (38.50%), and finishing (46.20%). Among the 60 craftsmen assessed through REBA, squatting, crossed-leg sitting, one-leg-folded/one-leg-extended sitting, and sitting upright were observed across different activities. High REBA risk was particularly pronounced during bending, where 100% of the observed respondents across the reported gender and craft groups were classified in the high-risk category for both body sides. During splitting, stripping, weaving, and finishing, high-risk classifications were also frequently observed, particularly among squatting, crossed-leg, and one-leg-folded/one-leg-extended postures. A statistically significant association was found between age and type of adopted posture (χ² = 14.56, p = 0.006), whereas associations with gender (χ² = 5.34, p = 0.069) and work experience (χ² = 9.81, p = 0.279) were not significant. Post-hoc analysis showed that squatting was adopted significantly more frequently than expected among craftsmen aged 20–35 years (adjusted residual = +2.34, p < 0.05). Conclusion: Bamboo and cane weaving involve prolonged daily work, predominantly low-level sitting arrangements, constrained postures, and considerable ergonomic risk. The high prevalence of high-risk REBA classifications, particularly during bending, highlights the need for ergonomically appropriate sitting arrangements and workstation design. Incorporating suitable seating, posture modification, adequate rest pauses, task variation, and ergonomic awareness may help reduce postural strain and occupational discomfort and improve the safety and efficiency of traditional bamboo and cane weaving work.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Background/Objectives: The psychosocial and organizational demands of healthcare work intensify during public health crises, with implications for professional functioning. This study aimed to identify the occupational demands and workplace resources associated with professional functioning among pediatric hospital staff, using the Job Demands–Resources (JD-R) framework as the guiding theoretical model. Methods: A cross-sectional, mixed-methods study was conducted among 903 employees of a pediatric emergency hospital in 2024, using a custom questionnaire and thematic analysis of open-ended responses, interpreted through the JD-R framework. Multivariable logistic regression models assessed five occupational functioning outcomes, with workload, age, sex, tenure, occupational category, COVID-sector work, and relocation as predictors. Results: A significant workload increase was the most consistent predictor, associated with four of the five outcomes (aOR 2.04–7.16), and relocation was associated with three outcomes (aOR 1.70–2.49); COVID-sector assignment was not independently associated with the other four outcomes after correction for multiple testing, but was associated with lower odds of difficulty returning to work among infected staff (aOR 0.38). Thematic analysis identified seven themes aligned with the JD-R framework; most were significantly more frequent among COVID-sector staff after FDR correction, although a sensitivity analysis restricted to respondents who answered the open-ended item attenuated this pattern for several themes and reversed it for one. Quantitative–qualitative comparisons showed convergent associations across the constructs examined. Conclusions: Workload and organizational disruption were more consistently associated with impaired occupational functioning than formal sector assignment. These findings support the value of monitoring psychosocial workload indicators in occupational health surveillance and highlight team-level resources as a relevant direction for future prevention efforts.

Introduction. Occupational diseases remain an underreported public health problem. In Italy, national insurance claims provide a useful view of recognized occupational diseases, although they do not measure the full burden of disease in the workforce. Few studies have combined descriptive analysis of insurance claims with predictive modelling to assess factors associated with recognized impairment. Methods. We conducted a retrospective observational analysis of 310,189 occupational disease claims from the Italian National Institute for Insurance against Accidents at Work (INAIL) open data, covering the period 2020 to 2024. Multivariable linear regression was used to estimate associations between demographic, clinical, and occupational factors and the degree of impairment. Neural-network models with embedding layers were developed to classify claims with recognized impairment (>0%) and to predict impairment severity. Results. Musculoskeletal disorders represented the largest share of claims, whereas neoplasms and asbestos-related diseases were associated with the highest impairment. Diagnostic category and causal agent were the strongest predictors of severity among claims. The classification model achieved 98.15% accuracy and 99.99% sensitivity for recognized impairment. The regression model attained a mean absolute error of 2.31% and R2=0.71, outperforming the linear regression baseline R2=0.55). Conclusion. Combining descriptive epidemiology with machine learning yields actionable insights for prioritizing high-risk claims and supporting administrative decision-making in occupational health surveillance. These findings represent a proof of concept given inherent administrative data limitations, including underreporting, lack of workforce denominators, and potential data bias. Future developments should incorporate explainable artificial intelligence techniques to bridge the gap between predictive performance and clinical interpretability.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Introduction: Occupational health and safety (OHS) is governed by mandatory national regulations, whereas ISO 45001, the international standard for OHS management systems (OHSMS), is adopted voluntarily; yet the scientific literature on OHSMS remains insufficiently mapped. This study analyzed the scientific output and academic impact of research on OHSMS and ISO 45001 between 2018 and 2026. Method: A descriptive bibliometric study was conducted, adapted from PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-S. Scopus was searched using ("Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems" AND "ISO 45001") up to 24 August 2026; of 496 records identified, 350 documents were analyzed with Python and Bibliometrix. Results: Articles represented 64.9% of documents and 87.7% were in English. Annual output rose from 16 documents in 2018 to 67 in 2025; Indonesia, Portugal, and the Russian Federation were the most productive countries. Engineering predominated (40.6%), and 70% of documents reported no funding. Management systems and risk assessment were the main thematic axes, while safety culture, certification, and artificial intelligence appeared in the most recent period. Impact was moderate (7.36 citations per document; maximum author h-index = 5 within the corpus); the most cited document received 89 citations, and Safety Science (h-index = 9) was the most influential journal. Collaboration networks were fragmented. Conclusions: Research on OHSMS and ISO 45001 is growing but shows moderate academic impact and weak articulation of international collaboration. Practical Applications: Findings can help researchers and funders prioritize collaborative, funded studies on ISO 45001 implementation and the empirical evaluation of emerging digital and artificial intelligence applications.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces
keywords: occupational health and safety management system

documents.abstract: This paper examined public health and occupational health in Nigeria with focus on laws, institutions, and changing dynamics. Historically, public health governance in Nigeria was anchored on the Public Health Act of 1917 and later the National Health Act, 2014, while occupational health was regulated under the Factories Act, 1987 and Employees’ Compensation Act, 2010. Key institutions such as the Federal Ministry of Health, NCDC, and NESREA were established to coordinate health responses. However, the sector faced issues including weak enforcement of laws, poor funding, fragmented institutional mandates, inadequate occupational safety compliance, and rising burden of communicable and non-communicable diseases. Challenges were compounded by urbanization, informal sector growth, and weak data systems, which limited effective regulation. The paper concluded that despite reforms, implementation gaps persisted. It recommended harmonization of health laws, strengthening of regulatory institutions, increased budgetary allocation, and adoption of risk-based inspection to improve public and occupational health outcomes in Nigeria.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND: Occupational exposures involving heavy manual lifting, prolonged standing, and physically demanding labor represent established risk factors for abdominal wall hernia development. Saudi Arabia’s labor force, characterized by a substantial manual workforce concentrated in construction, manufacturing, and agriculture, may carry elevated occupational hernia risk, yet population-level analyses quantifying these associations are absent from the literature. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to characterize the prevalence of self-reported abdominal wall hernias by occupational category among Saudi working-age adults, quantify the association between specific occupational exposures and hernia risk, and assess geographic and demographic variations in occupationally attributed hernia burden. METHODS: This cross-sectional descriptive study analyzed secondary data from the Saudi Health Interview Survey 2018 ( n = 10,735 adults aged 18–65 years), Saudi General Authority for Statistics Labor Force Survey 2018–2023, and Saudi Ministry of Health Annual Statistical Yearbooks. Hernia prevalence was stratified by occupational category using the International Standard Classification of Occupations. The specific exposures analyzed included heavy manual lifting, prolonged standing, and physically demanding labor. Comparative analyses and prevalence ratios (PRs) were calculated. Reporting followed strengthening the reporting of observational studies in epidemiology guidelines. RESULTS: The overall self-reported hernia prevalence was 8.3% among working-age adults. Manual laborers demonstrated the highest hernia prevalence (14.7%), followed by construction and extraction workers (13.2%) and agricultural workers (11.8%), compared to 4.1% among professional/managerial workers. Hernia prevalence was significantly associated with daily heavy lifting exceeding 20 kg (PR: 2.84; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.31–3.49), prolonged standing exceeding 6 h per day (PR: 1.76; 95% CI: 1.42–2.18), and duration of occupational exposure exceeding 10 years (PR: 2.21; 95% CI: 1.87–2.61). Male sex, age 45–65 years, and concurrent obesity amplified occupational hernia risk. Geographic analysis revealed highest hernia procedure rates in regions with concentrated industrial and agricultural workforces. CONCLUSIONS: Occupational exposures, particularly heavy manual lifting and prolonged standing, are significantly associated with abdominal wall hernia prevalence in Saudi Arabia’s working-age population. Targeted workplace prevention programs, ergonomic interventions, pre-employment screening, and enhanced access to hernia repair services for manual labor sectors represent priority occupational health policy actions.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) is a crucial aspect of preventing workplace accidents and illnesses, particularly during high-risk vessel unloading operations at the Kutaraja Oceanic Fishing Port (OFP) in Banda Aceh. Inadequate implementation of safety programs, such as hazard identification, risk analysis, and risk control, is a primary cause of workplace accidents in this sector. This study aimed to identify activities and analyze occupational safety risks associated with the unloading process of purse seine vessels at OFP Kutaraja over one month, focusing on seven vessels. The methodology involved direct observation, interviews with crew members, and data analysis using the Job Safety Analysis (JSA) approach. Risk assessment was conducted using a risk matrix that factored in both severity and probability. The results indicate that the unloading operation comprises three main stages: pre-unloading, the unloading process, and post-unloading. Each stage presents varying levels of risk, ranging from "Acceptable" to "Unacceptable". The highest risks were associated with handling fish-filled brail nets and transporting the catch, activities that carry the potential for serious accidents. Contributing risk factors included the lack of use of personal protective equipment (PPE), suboptimal work procedures, and unsafe working conditions. Safety during vessel unloading operations could be improved through regular training, increased PPE usage, and the implementation of a JSA-based risk control system.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Background: Watch repairing involves prolonged near-vision activity, monocular loupe use, sustained convergence, awkward postures, and repetitive fine motor movements, potentially contributing to ocular strain. The ocular and ergonomic impact of such occupations has not yet been documented. Objective: To study the ocular stress profile along with ergonomics risk factors among male watchmakers from Kolkata, India. Methods: This comparative cross-sectional study included 140 men aged 40–50 years, comprising 70 watchmakers with over 15 years of occupational exposure and 70 controls. Visual pain was assessed using a visual analogue scale (VAS), near point of convergence (NPC) and accommodation using the RAF rule, fusional vergence using a prism bar, ocular movements using a synoptophore, intraocular pressure (IOP) using non-contact tonometry, and visual acuity using a Snellen chart. Fundus photography and ergonomic assessments were also performed. Data were analysed using independent-samples t-tests (SPSS version 26; p<0.05). Results: Watchmakers exhibited significantly greater visual pain (7.29±0.58 cm vs. 3.81±0.30 cm; p<0.001) and receded NPC (16.57±1.51 cm vs. 7.86±1.35 cm; p<0.001), both remaining significant after Holm correction. Adduction was reduced (p=0.010), whereas IOP was higher in both eyes (p=0.044). Visual acuity and anthropometric differences were statistically insignificant. Major ergonomic concerns included inadequate rest periods, monocular loupe use, postural strain, and hand discomfort. Conclusion: Prolonged monocular near work by watchmakers can lead to convergence insufficiency-like symptoms, increased eye pain, and increased intraocular pressure. It is necessary for ergonomic measures such as using bi-ocular devices and proper work rest cycles and eye screenings to be taken.

Computational biologists increasingly delegate substantial analyses to AI agents in long-horizon, multi-turn sessions, yet most benchmarks of agents' bioinformatics capabilities pose a single short task with a single-shot prompt. We present OmicsBench, a long-horizon, multi-turn bioinformatics benchmark for AI agents. Each of its 97 tasks links dependent subtasks into a directed acyclic graph, for 662 underlying subtasks in all. Each subtask is posed as one user turn and graded deterministically against an answer key, with optional in-context feedback on incorrect answers. Across 12 models on three harnesses, the slowest agent averages 3.6 hours per task, and no combination comes near saturating the benchmark, with mean scores of 0.43 to 0.57 out of a possible 1 without in-context feedback and 0.54 to 0.67 with it. Multi-turn evaluation also uncovers behavior that single-shot prompts cannot, as agents score lower on subtasks that depend on earlier subtasks, and in-context feedback helps agents recover some of that loss. Because deterministic scoring gives no qualitative account of how an agent failed, we also introduce an unsupervised failure mode discovery pipeline that describes, embeds, and clusters agents' failed attempts to surface emergent failure modes. Applied to OmicsBench, this pipeline exposes qualitative shortcomings in how agents carry out bioinformatics analyses, ranging from agents applying their own statistical filters in place of the specified ones to agents writing whole answers from memory.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Aerial robots operating near people must treat a pedestrian, a parked car, and a wall differently, yet conventional perception--planning stacks reduce all of them to occupied geometry---a \emph{human-aware safety gap} in which category-specific clearance is unavailable to the planner and temporary occlusions remove pedestrian-specific constraints from its map. We present a modular, fully onboard pipeline that closes this gap by turning visual observations into context-dependent safety constraints for real-time UAV navigation. A shared BLIP encoder drives scene captioning and text-conditioned segmentation, which is fused with depth to localize obstacles in 3D. Obstacle-specific risk is inferred by a lightweight LLM (Qwen-2.5-0.5B) stabilized with retrieval-augmented generation and grammar-constrained decoding that restricts its output to a planner-compatible JSON schema. The LLM reasons once per object category rather than per frame: its verdicts are cached per class, so previously seen categories are resolved without inference and new ones trigger a fresh retrieval-grounded query; detections are additionally given persistent identities and held in the map across occlusions. The perception pipeline runs at 10\,Hz on a Jetson Orin NX, while fallback LLM queries take approximately 0.8\,s and remain off the control-critical path. In Gazebo, low-altitude urban navigation among pedestrians and vehicles shows a roughly $3\times$ reduction in collision events over a geometric planner, and semantics-aware landing among moving actors raises success from 34\% to 96\%. The 224-pixel encoder input limits reliable small-object perception at range; conservative pedestrian margins and short-term persistence mitigate this limitation during navigation.

Learning from experience requires recovering reusable knowledge and determining when it applies to a new situation. We introduce OntoAct, a hypothesis-based neuro-symbolic framework built on ontological abstraction. OntoAct turns individual experiences into axioms over entity types, relations, and conditions, making their underlying patterns reusable across situations. A large language model (LLM) uses this world knowledge to propose hypotheses and actions, while a symbolic verifier assesses their supporting conditions against current observations. Verification identifies missing evidence, and new observations and intervention outcomes update hypothesis assessments and guide subsequent actions. We also introduce Tacit-FLE, a benchmark built on the Factorio Learning Environment (FLE) for diagnosing and repairing hidden faults in existing factories using inherited operational records. Its synthetic maintenance corpus distributes evidence across records, and an executed repair may leave the fault unresolved, requiring agents to reassess their diagnoses through interaction. Across Tacit-FLE, Mars, and ALFWorld, OntoAct achieves leading task performance with efficient interaction and inference.

This thesis reconstructs and critically evaluates Operation Dark Clark, a Russia-origin influence operation that OpenAI reportedly disrupted and publicly documented on 8 October 2026. It assesses the operation as the first influence campaign ever classified by the company in Category 5 of the IO Breakout Scale—its highest rating for a disrupted operation—and the most complex false-front identity it had dismantled in two and a half years of systematic reporting. The operation combined generative artificial intelligence with classical intelligence tradecraft. It recruited unwitting employees in Latin America to staff a seemingly legitimate organization called the “Social Research Center” (SRC), which was controlled through a fabricated persona named “Mia Clark.” Her published corpus comprised more than sixty original research articles examining public opinion on BRICS and comparing the Brazilian economy under Presidents Jair Bolsonaro and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Drawing on an open-source intelligence (OSINT) verification protocol that distinguishes documented and verified facts from attributed claims and editorial speculation, the thesis traces the operation’s activities across Argentina, Bolivia, Ecuador, Peru, Panama, and Brazil. It reconstructs the operation’s institutional lineage, from Soviet active measures through the Internet Research Agency, PeaceData (2020), and the Prigozhin-linked “Politology”/“La Compañia” network, reportedly now under the control of Russia’s Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR). The study situates the case within the broader industrialization of AI-enabled information confrontation, examining the contemporaneous Iranian “Bogus Bylines” operation and the transnational Pravda network. A dedicated chapter investigates the October 2026 Ukrainian strikes on Yandex data centers and the observed 94% collapse in automated traffic across the Yandex network, cautioning against unwarranted causal interpretations of the relationship between these events. The thesis argues that Dark Clark represents a doctrinal evolution from platform-based amplification toward institutional laundering: the introduction of synthetic or co-opted authority into established media organizations and academic institutions. It contends that effective democratic resilience requires a multilayered response combining platform transparency, institutional source verification, provenance standards, and robust fact-checking capacity. The analysis deliberately refrains from endorsing the unverified assertion circulating in Brazilian political commentary that the operation materially influenced Brazilian electoral outcomes.
topics: European and Russian Geopolitical Military Strategies

documents.abstract: Remote ID has emerged as a foundational capability for enabling accountability, situational awareness, and scalable integration of unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) into the national airspace. While current regulatory frameworks emphasize Remote ID as a key component of future UAS operations, limited discussion has focused on how Remote ID data performs under real operational monitoring conditions. This presentation examines the practical reliability of Remote ID for real-time UAS surveillance and highlights several operational limitations that affect tracking continuity, detection confidence, and airspace awareness. The study presents a data-driven evaluation framework developed to analyze high frequency Remote ID observations alongside external UAS detection and telemetry data streams. The framework incorporates second-level temporal synchronization, geospatial matching, duplicate-event handling, and event-driven detection analysis to assess how inconsistencies in Remote ID broadcasts influence monitoring performance. Attention is given to issues such as timestamp irregularities, intermittent signal loss, identity ambiguity, and spatial inaccuracies resulting from differing positional reference systems and broadcast conditions. Results demonstrate that even small temporal or positional inconsistencies can significantly impact real-time surveillance reliability, particularly in dense or safety-sensitive operational environments. The presentation further discusses how these limitations may affect counter-UAS operations, enforcement workflows, Unmanned Aircraft System Traffic Management (UTM) integration, and broader airspace safety initiatives. Rather than positioning Remote ID as a standalone surveillance solution, the findings support a layered monitoring architecture in which Remote ID is integrated with complementary sensing modalities such as radar, RF detection, and network-based tracking systems. In addition to identifying operational gaps, the presentation proposes several recommendations aimed at improving the reliability and interoperability of Remote ID based monitoring systems. These include improved timestamp standardization, enhanced broadcast consistency requirements, and more rigorous validation methodologies for evaluating real-time detection performance. The goal of this work is to provide government, industry, and academic stakeholders with a practical assessment of the current capabilities and limitations of Remote ID as the UAS ecosystem continues to expand.

This praxis investigates how artificial intelligence (AI) governance can be integrated into the cybersecurity compliance workflows of United States defense small and mid-sized enterprises (SMEs). These firms are navigating the transition to the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) 2.0 program and the foundational requirements of National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Special Publication (SP) 800-171. Existing AI risk guidance, such as the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF), does not provide implementation-focused direction suited to the resource constraints of smaller firms. This praxis therefore describes a control mapping method consistent with the overlay logic of NIST's Control Overlays for Securing AI Systems (COSAIS) concept paper. It uses that method to develop the Modular AI Governance Framework (MAGF), a "comply once, satisfy many" governance framework and toolkit. My research uses a convergent mixed-methods design guided by five research questions. Four ask how practitioners map AI risk categories to control families, which families they identify most often, how feasible they judge lightweight governance artifacts to be, and what barriers and enablers shape implementation. The fifth asks to what extent the resulting framework is practical, scalable, and audit-aligned. In the first phase, 38 practitioners mapped six AI risk categories onto the 14 NIST SP 800-171 control families through a structured survey. They prioritized "auditability gaps" in data integrity and model transparency, yet many reported lacking the specialized staff to document these areas manually. Qualitative analysis of their open-ended responses produced eight empirically grounded design requirements, including control family anchoring, traceability-first evidence, change control for probabilistic systems, and a dual-purpose evidence pattern. Inspired by operational "playbooks," the MAGF defines governance tasks as structured modules with goals, actions, and lightweight evidence artifacts. The modules model the work already required in defense cybersecurity and span the AI lifecycle from initiation and data collection to production deployment and monitoring. A prompt library provides engineered prompts for generative AI chatbot tools like Google's Gemini and Microsoft's Copilot to support human-reviewed drafting of artifacts such as bias assessment records and model/prompt change logs. No output of that prompt library was evaluated in this study. I evaluated the framework through a structured expert review rather than a measured field deployment. A panel of 13 qualified reviewers, six of whom identified primarily as assessors, rated the framework and its artifacts against defined criteria. The results were encouraging but bounded. Reviewers judged the framework relevant, clear, and valuable as assessment evidence. Their reservations centered on the feasibility of the most measurement-intensive artifacts for the smallest firms. Only 30.8% of reviewers were favorable on scalability, which marks the boundary of what this study establishes. An illustrative estimate anchored to published federal compliance cost figures and peer-reviewed evidence on generative writing productivity suggests a meaningful reduction in recurring drafting effort while human review remains constant. The estimate is not a measurement, and it does not assert that any requirement or practice is satisfied. It also shows that careful coordination is needed to keep documentation bloat and fatigue from eroding the benefit and slowing certification. This praxis contributes a method for compliance-aligned and resource-optimized AI governance design and applies it to build an integrated toolkit for defense SMEs. Future work can examine the generative AI assistance in greater detail and apply the framework to other emerging regulatory environments. The method offers a replicable template for integrating emerging technologies into highly regulated and risk-averse operations, helping small firms remain competitive while safeguarding national security.

Enterprises have moved large language model applications from pilot projects into production systems handling customer conversations, internal knowledge retrieval, and increasingly autonomous agentic workflows, introducing a risk surface that differs materially from what conventional application security programs address. OWASP has responded with the Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications, most recently revised in its 2025 edition, and a newly published Top 10 for Agentic Applications covering autonomous, tool-using systems. These taxonomies name and prioritize risk but leave engineering teams to translate categories such as prompt injection or excessive agency into controls that fit an existing cloud-native delivery pipeline. This paper proposes a reference architecture and implementation framework mapping each of the ten OWASP LLM Top 10 2025 categories to specific, deployable controls built on commonly used cloud primitives: managed model gateways, service mesh identity, retrieval-augmented generation pipelines, and continuous delivery tooling. The framework is informed by production engineering practice with retrieval-augmented generation and agentic workloads on Kubernetes using a managed foundation model service. Five real, publicly documented incidents, including a corporate data leak, a manipulated dealership chatbot, a legal ruling on chatbot liability, an indirect prompt injection exfiltration attack, and a zero-click vulnerability in a widely used enterprise copilot, are analyzed against the proposed controls to show where the framework would have reduced impact or prevented the incident outright. A four-stage maturity model helps organizations sequence adoption. Open challenges discussed include the immaturity of evaluation tooling for non-deterministic systems and the persistent tension between guardrail thoroughness and production latency.

With the frequent occurrence of public health emergencies such as the COVID-19 pandemic, the allocation and coordinated use of emergency supplies around the world have generated large amounts of waste, thus creating an urgent need to improve and optimize emergency reverse logistics systems. This study proposes a model for optimizing waste recycling vehicle routing to address waste management issues. The model provides ideal transportation solutions for the simultaneous collection of general waste and medical waste. Based on the characteristics of the model, an artificial intelligence algorithm—i.e., an improved genetic algorithm based on bit-string-matching coding and a field restriction operator—is designed and compared with an ant colony optimization algorithm. A synthetic numerical example inspired by the situation in Wuhan, China, is tested using relevant data on the locations of 18 medical facilities mentioned in existing case studies of the COVID-19 pandemic to verify the effectiveness and practicality of the model and the algorithm. This study provides support for decision-making regarding optimization strategies for the reverse logistics of waste generated during public health emergencies.

We examine how expertise, evidence and authority are organised in the international governance of Artificial Intelligence (AI), and what this reveals about the practice of science diplomacy. Science-diplomacy scholarship has become increasingly attentive to the political character of expertise and to the ways knowledge is mobilised within international governance. Yet less attention has been paid to the organisational practices through which such knowledge is brokered within governance processes. Drawing on documentary analysis and 23 semi-structured interviews, we compare UNESCO’s Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence and the EU AI Act. Through an abductive analysis, we develop Organisational Knowledge Brokerage (OKB) to explain how a contested object such as AI is made workable for governance. We identify four connected practices through which this occurs: stabilising the governance object, legitimising expertise, building authority and operationalising governance. These practices took different forms under contrasting institutional mandates and governing capacities. UNESCO worked through global intergovernmental standard-setting and implementation support, while the EU combined supranational regulation with expert advice and Member State coordination. Across both cases, OKB also produced a cross-cutting process that we term normative translation, through which contested values acquired practical meaning in definitions, assessments and procedures. We show how this brokerage allowed each organisation to establish workable and revisable settlements around AI under conditions of technological uncertainty and dispersed authority. The article therefore develops a practice-oriented account of science diplomacy as organisational work through which knowledge, values and institutional authority are assembled for collective action in international technology governance.
keywords: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence

documents.abstract: Introduction Coproparasitological analysis in zoo animals is essential for preventing parasitic diseases, which can compromise conservation efforts and pose occupational health risks. This study aimed to characterize the endoparasitic fauna detected in fecal samples from mammals, birds, and reptiles maintained at the Getúlio Vargas Zoobotanical Park, Salvador, Bahia, Brazil. Methods Fecal samples were examined using four complementary coproparasitological methods: the direct method, spontaneous sedimentation, Willis flotation, and Mini-FLOTAC®. Results Of the samples (N = 144), 52.8% were positive. Among these, 80.3% harbored nematodes, 23.7% protozoa, 13.2% cestodes, and 10.5% trematodes, with 26.3% presenting mixed infections. In primates, coccidia, Strongyloides spp., Bertiella spp., and Platynosomum spp. were observed; in carnivores, Strongyloides spp. and Oxyuridae; in Artiodactyla, Balantioides spp., Trichuris spp., and Strongyloides spp.; in Perissodactyla, Balantioides spp. and Strongyloidea; and in Didelphimorphia, Eimeria spp., Cruzia spp., and Aspidodera spp. In birds, Capillaria spp., Isospora spp., and cestodes were identified; in reptiles, Nyctotherus spp. and Balantioides spp. were detected. Discussion This study reports, for the first time, the occurrence of Strongyloides spp. in Ateles marginatus and Leontopithecus chrysomelas, Bertiella spp. in Callicebus barbarabrownae and Saimiri sciureus , and Capillaria spp. in Amazona rhodocorytha, Eupsittula aurea , and Diopsittca nobilis .
