documents.abstract: Traditional advertising methods, such as paper posters, banners, and hoardings, require manual design, printing, installation, and maintenance. These activities increase operational effort, material consumption, and the difficulty of updating advertisements. This paper presents SmartAds, a web-based artificial intelligence-powered digital advertisement management platform developed to simplify advertisement creation, pricing, payment-record management, approval, scheduling, and display. The system enables users to generate promotional descriptions and slogans from product details using large language model services. A fallback mechanism involving Groq, an optional local Ollama model, and rule-based generation supports content creation when an AI service is unavailable. Users can select poster or video formats, choose display slots, calculate advertisement costs, and track their submissions. Administrators can approve or reject advertisements before they are scheduled for display. The platform also includes payment-record management, receipt generation, notifications, optional AI avatar-video generation through D-ID, and a browser-based virtual LED display. SmartAds was implemented using Python, Flask, SQLAlchemy, HTML, Bootstrap, and JavaScript. Functional testing documented in the project report covered 45 test cases, all reported as passing. The system demonstrates the feasibility of integrating AI-assisted content generation with digital advertisement workflow management in a controlled proof-of-concept environment.

The scheduling of surgical procedures is a vital and intricate aspect of hospital operations, significantly impacting patient outcomes, financial success, and clinician welfare.Traditional manual scheduling techniques are inadequate for managing the dynamic and unpredictable characteristics of the operating room (OR) environment, resulting in staff fatigue, increased overtime expenses, and a decline in care quality.This study presents a comprehensive artificial intelligence (AI) framework that utilises predictive analytics, multi-objective optimisation, and natural language processing to create dynamic, efficient, and equitable surgical schedules.The technology utilises a continuous feedback loop, assimilating historical and real-time data to optimise operational efficiency while considering human aspects.Conceptual analysis indicates Smart Surgical Scheduling: An AI-Enabled Framework for Operating Room Efficiency and Quality of Care https://iaeme.com/Home/journal/IJCET

Background: Due to structural inequities, many migrant workers face adverse health outcomes potentially exposing them to long-term pain issues. However, the extent of current knowledge on chronic pain (>3 months) in this population is unclear. As labor migration policies evolve toward less protective measures, it is essential to gain insights into the experiences and drivers of chronic pain among migrant workers. Aims: Drawing on the theoretical framework of intersectionality, this scoping review aimed to synthesize existing knowledge on chronic pain among migrant workers in Canada and the United States. More precisely, we examined evidence related to epidemiology, treatments, lived experiences, and the role of social and structural determinants. Methods: This review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology for scoping reviews. A search of four databases was followed by a screening and extraction procedure involving four researchers. Relevant findings were reported through quantified and narrative syntheses. Results: This scoping review highlights a major gap in understanding pain chronicity among migrant workers. Nine studies met the eligibility criteria. Most studies have focused on occupational health outcomes. Definitions of chronic pain are inconsistent. Only one qualitative study examined migrant workers' pain trajectories beyond workplace settings. Social and structural determinants were underscored in all studies, including poor working conditions, socioeconomic precarity, unfavorable labor market structure, restrictive immigration policies, racism and discrimination, and gendered inequities. Conclusions: This review invites researchers and policymakers to move beyond occupational health approaches to fully appraise and tackle the intersecting structural and political drivers exposing migrant workers to lifelong experiences of chronic pain.

The objective of this study was to determine the influence of social networking use, informal workplace learning, and personal professional development on teachers' attitudes and beliefs towards ICT adoption among public secondary school teachers in Region XI, Philippines. Standardized survey questionnaires were adopted and contextualized to suit the regional educational setting. The instruments were administered to 417 randomly selected teachers using stratified random sampling. This study employed a quantitative, non-experimental research design, using means, Pearson's r, and Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) for data analysis. The results revealed generally low to very low levels of social networking usage, informal workplace learning, personal professional development, and attitudes and beliefs toward ICT adoption. Despite these modest levels, significant positive relationships were found between social networking use and teachers' attitudes toward ICT adoption, as well as between personal professional development and these attitudes. Furthermore, the structural equation modeling results indicated that the three independent variables significantly influenced teachers' attitudes and beliefs toward ICT adoption, with social networking usage emerging as the strongest predictor among the constructs. The findings underscore the importance of enhancing digital engagement, strengthening informal learning cultures, and providing sustained professional development initiatives to foster more positive attitudes and stronger readiness for ICT integration in schools.

Academic motivation in higher education constitutes a multidimensional construct shaped by structural conditions that influence students’ academic performance, persistence, and educational trajectories. In contexts characterized by persistent social inequalities, understanding how socioeconomic status (SES) configures motivational processes is essential for the development of university policies aimed at equity and educational sustainability. The purpose of this study was to conduct a critical synthesis of international evidence on the mechanisms through which socioeconomic factors influences academic motivation in higher education during the period period 2017–2020 and 2022–2025. A systematic review was carried out in accordance with PRISMA guidelines to ensure methodological rigor, transparency, and replicability. The literature search was conducted in the Scopus database using structured Boolean search equations. After applying predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, 33 empirical studies were selected for the final analysis. The results of the systematic synthesis reveal sustained growth in scientific output and progressive geographic diversification of the field. Cross-sectional quantitative studies predominate, employing regression models and structural analyses to examine the relationship between parental educational level, financial support, and intrinsic motivation or academic engagement. In addition, several studies incorporate mediating variables such as self-efficacy, institutional integration, and sense of belonging, revealing non-linear explanatory configurations. Overall, the evidence indicates that the influence of socioeconomic status operates through both direct and indirect mechanisms linked to cultural capital and institutional resources. This review identifies key theoretical convergences as well as recurrent methodological limitations within the field. Finally, the findings underscore the need for longitudinal studies and multilevel approaches to deepen the understanding of motivational inequalities in higher education.

TITLE OF THE INVENTION:SOFTWARE-ONLY NEURAL-SYNCHRONIZED ACCESS PROTOCOL (NZAP) FOR MIXED REALITY HEADSETS FEATURING MULTIMODAL SENSOR FUSION, DYNAMIC ERGONOMIC SCALING, AND LOCAL ENCLAVE ZERO-KNOWLEDGE SECURITY APPLICANT / ASSIGNEE (100% OWNER):Meta Platforms, Inc., 1 Hacker Way, Menlo Park, CA 94025, USA — via Assignment of Rights by Dr. Michael Allan Bahtaji — Represented by Facebook Philippines, 11F One World Place, BGC, Taguig INVENTOR FOR ACKNOWLEDGEMENT ONLY:Dr. Michael Allan Bahtaji, Technological University of the Philippines - Manila — No Ownership, No Royalty — Goodwill Defensive Assignment ABSTRACT:A software-orchestrated Neural-Synchronized Access Protocol (NZAP) for head-mounted mixed reality displays (HMDs) that replaces vulnerable external physical controllers and wireless Bluetooth HID peripherals with secure multimodal sensor fusion of optical targeting orientation vectors and wearable electromyography (EMG). The protocol establishes spatial targeting coordinates via optical head-pose orientation vectors or optional eye-tracking arrays, and captures discrete interaction triggers via EMG motor-unit action potentials (MUAPs) synchronized across a 15ms to 50ms temporal coincidence window. Biometric calibration matrices are vectorized and locked inside a hardware Trusted Execution Environment (TEE), purging raw telemetry immediately post-vectorization. Operating within an air-gapped local memory execution boundary, third-party applications receive strictly zero-knowledge abstract input events (e.g., KeyDown, PointerClick). By dynamically throttling high-overhead computer-vision hand-tracking GPU/NPU inference cycles during active temporal coincidence states, system power consumption is significantly reduced without requiring dedicated auxiliary coprocessors. Many pharmacological compounds suffer from poor aqueous solubility, variable bioavailability, fast degradation, unfavorable biodistribution and dose-related side effects, which restrict their therapeutic efficacy. Conventional dosage forms may not achieve the appropriate drug concentrations within the therapeutic window, necessitating the development of improved delivery platforms. Lipid-based nanocarriers, especially solid lipid nanoparticles (SLNs) and nanostructured lipid carriers (NLCs), provide intriguing methods owing to their biocompatibility, biodegradability and formulation diversity. SLNs are composed of a largely solid lipid matrix supported by surfactants, while NLCs are a mixture of solid and liquid lipids that form a less ordered matrix with more drug accommodation and less drug ejection during storage. This review critically discusses recent advances, with emphasis on literature published during 2021–2026, on the evolution, classification, structural characteristics, formulation components, preparation and characterization, drug-loading and release mechanisms, biological fate, surface engineering, administration routes, and therapeutic applications of SLNs and NLCs. Special attention is paid to safety, regulatory issues, scale-up, commercialization and emerging technologies including artificial intelligence-assisted optimization and microfluidic production. [There has been] considerable preclinical progress but little clinical translation. Long term stability, reproducible large scale manufacturing, regulatory uniformity, and rigorous clinical validation are significant difficulties that need to be systematically investigated.

Spatial reasoning is a key cognitive foundation for children’s STEM learning, yet existing tools focus on 2D tasks or programming logic, with limited integration of multidimensional spatial reasoning, embodied interaction, and feedback. We developed SpaceMates, a tangible programming game combining tabletop robots with 3D-printed blocks for children aged 7–10. Children construct 3D structures, plan routes with height variations, and compare intended and executed paths through robot feedback. Based on developmental trajectories of spatial skills in middle childhood and the Spatial Reasoning Instrument (SRI), we designed tasks for ages 7–8 and 9–10. In study with 30 participants, we examined within- and between-condition changes. Unadjusted tests suggested MR and SV gains for ages 7–8 and SO gains for ages 9–10 in SpaceMates, with greater SO gains than Baseline. In Holm-adjusted analyses, only the pre–post SO change among participants aged 9–10 remained statistically significant; after adjustment, no between-condition gain comparison remained statistically significant. Behavioral analyses characterized interaction patterns.
